..(This Evening Through Saturday)
Issued at 1230 PM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Analysis (19z or 1 pm MDT): The longwave flow over the CONUS
remains in a trough (west) and ridge (east) pattern with much of
the northern Plains sitting between these two features allowing
for the SE winds to continue across the region and allowing for
our moisture source to be both the monsoon moisture pooled across
the Desert SW and portions of the Gulf. This has aided into the
formation of the foggy conditions we have seen Friday and again
this morning. This trend will continue and we should see patchy
fog again on Sunday morning. Latest VIS Satellite image shows most
of the fog has dissipated across much of western SD and with skies
becoming scattered to clear. With the modest WAA (Warm Air
Advection) into the region temperatures have moderated quickly
over the past several hours. Current forecast high temperatures
today look on track with much of the region seeing temperatures in
the low to mid 60s with pockets of lower 70's possible.

Sunday: After what could be some patchy areas of fog to start the
day, we can expect another quiet and mild day on Monday with
continued breezy southeasterly winds. Temperatures will again warm
into the 60s across much of the area. The indicator of the shift
in the weather will be the increase in mid to high clouds as we
progress through the day on Sunday. We are tracking a large area
of low pressure that will be slowly moving through the
Intermountain West on Sunday and this will be the system that will
bring unsettled weather to the area on Monday and Tuesday.

Models show a strengthening Colorado Low system moving into
southern SD Monday morning. Some discrepancies remain on the 
exact location of low pressure system by overall most models do 
show a closed low somewhere in central SD Monday morning. This 
system will be bring rain and wind to western SD. Focusing first 
on the wind. This low pressure system will continue to deepen as 
it moves into SD and become sandwiched between two ridges with one
remaining over the east coast and on developing across the west 
coast a belt of strong NW winds develops on the backside of the 
low and comes directly over much of western SD. Some of models 
that were showing the highest winds have since backed off a bit 
and have come into better agreement with most of the ensemble 
members with current forecast agreement falling in the 45 to 55 
mph range for wind gusts on Monday. If this transpires then Wind 
Advisories will be hoisted. With the feature not developed in this
forecast package and location of the low still in question, no 
wind highlights will be issued this afternoon.

This system will have decent amount of moisture so we are
confidence for high end precipitation chances across much of the
area on Monday and this should fall in the form of rain for much
of the plains and Black Hill Foothills. The best chances for some
light snow will be in the highest elevations of the Black Hills.
There will be a sharp gradient in precipitation totals which again
will depend on the exact track of the low itself, add in the
expected downslope wind component and this could eat into some of
the totals in these areas. Nonetheless much of area should see
some accumulating rains with the highest totals at this time 
being for locations along and east of the river. 

In the wake of the main system on Monday, a fast moving system
dives out of ND and pushes through the area quickly on Tuesday.
This will bring some cooler temperatures to the region and keep
those breezy NW winds in place but these won't be as strong as
what we will with the system on Monday. Beyond Tuesday, the rest 
of the week looks to be quiet with nice fall temperatures expected
before we potentially look at another system coming in just in 
time for next weekend.
